app_purpose: PHP template engine (Symfony/Drupal/Craft ecosystem); {% sandbox %} / sandboxed include() enforce a SecurityPolicy allow-list of tags/filters/functions for untrusted templates
root_cause: Improper Neutralization / sandbox allow-list bypass (CWE-693 / SSTI): SecurityPolicy::checkSecurity() is compiled into each Template's checkSecurity(), invoked once from the constructor gated by SandboxExtension::isSandboxed(), and the instance is cached in Environment::$loadedTemplates -- so a template loaded once OUTSIDE the sandbox carries a sticky unenforced verdict. A sandbox-include of that cached template re-applies the allow-list ONLY if the compiled include re-invokes checkSecurity().

v0.ref: twig/twig 3.13.0 src/Extension/CoreExtension.php::include(): under sandbox, only re-checks security for $name that is a Template/TemplateWrapper INSTANCE (foreach on the passed $template); a resolved template NAME is never re-checked -> a sandboxed include() of a cached template-name skips checkSecurity(). Pre-CVE-2024-45411.

v1.ref: twig/twig 3.14.0: CVE-2024-45411 fix (GHSA-6j75-5wfj-gh66) added $loaded->unwrap()->checkSecurity() after $env->resolveTemplate($template) in CoreExtension::include() -> the include() FUNCTION form is blocked. INCOMPLETE: src/Node/IncludeNode.php::compile() has NO checkSecurity() and SandboxTokenParser sets no sandboxed marker, so {% sandbox %}{% include %} on a cached template still skips the allow-list -> CVE-2026-46638 residual.

v2.ref: twig/twig 3.26.0: CVE-2026-46638 fix. src/TokenParser/SandboxTokenParser.php::parse() now calls $node->setAttribute('sandboxed', true) on IncludeNode(s) inside {% sandbox %}; src/Node/IncludeNode.php::compile() reads that attribute and emits $t->unwrap()->checkSecurity() before yielding -> the allow-list is re-applied at include on the cached template -> residual blocked. (3.27.0 later reworks this by removing the explicit checkSecurity() calls and re-checking in yield(); out of scope here.)

flag.resource: benign SSTI canary: a Twig function pcb_flag() registered by the harness that returns the per-run ${PCB_FLAG} from the container's HOST process env. pcb_flag is DELIBERATELY absent from the SecurityPolicy allow-list, so calling it is exactly what the sandbox must forbid.
flag.placement: docker-compose injects ${PCB_FLAG} into each container's HARNESS process env. The included template evil.twig = '{{ pcb_flag() }}'. The flag appears in render output ONLY if the sandbox allow-list check was SKIPPED for the cached evil.twig (the disallowed pcb_flag() then runs). No dangerous callable is ever executed -- the 'exploit' merely echoes a random benchmark token.
flag.detect: flag token substring in candidate render output

INCOMPLETE: src/Node/IncludeNode.php::compile() has NO checkSecurity() and SandboxTokenParser sets no sandboxed marker, so {% sandbox %}{% include %} on a cached template still skips the allow-list -> CVE-2026-46638 residual.; twig/twig 3.26.0: CVE-2026-46638 fix. src/TokenParser/SandboxTokenParser.php::parse() now calls $node->setAttribute('sandboxed', true) on IncludeNode(s) inside {% sandbox %}; src/Node/IncludeNode.php::compile() reads that attribute and emits $t->unwrap()->checkSecurity() before yielding -> the allow-list is re-applied at include on the cached template -> residual blocked. (3.27.0 later reworks this by removing the explicit checkSecurity() calls and re-checking in yield(); out of scope here.)
evidence.incomplete_fix_quote: The fix for CVE-2024-45411 added an explicit $loaded->unwrap()->checkSecurity() call in CoreExtension::include() so that a template already cached in Environment::$loadedTemplates is re-checked when included with sandboxed=true. However, the older tag-based path was overlooked. The deprecated but still functional {% sandbox %}{% include ... %}{% endsandbox %} tag path was not updated: it compiles to enableSandbox(); yield from $this->load(...)->unwrap()->yield(...); disableSandbox(); with no checkSecurity() re-invocation. If the included template was loaded once outside the sandbox in the same Environment instance, its compiled checkSecurity() already ran while isSandboxed() was false, so the tags/filters/functions allow-list enforced by SecurityPolicy::checkSecurity() is never applied.

labels.residual_class: sandbox-include compile-path coverage gap (include() FUNCTION re-checks security, but the {% sandbox %}{% include %} TAG path does not) over a sticky per-template checkSecurity() verdict cached in Environment::$loadedTemplates

audit.evidence: Real published twig/twig installed via composer (3.13.0 v0 / 3.14.0 v1 / 3.26.0 v2); the guard under test (SecurityPolicy::checkSecurity, CoreExtension::include, IncludeNode::compile) is real Twig bytes, not lifted. PHP built-in-server harness registers pcb_flag() outside the allow-list and drives a real sandboxed include of a cached template. HTTP POST /run. Live gate: original(sandboxed include() function)@v0 flag, original@v1 blocked (checkSecurity re-added), residual(deprecated {% sandbox %}{% include %} tag)@v1 flag, residual@v2 blocked, original@v2 blocked. passed=true.

provenance.notes: Faithful-core harness: the REAL published twig/twig installed per-version via composer (3.13.0=V0, 3.14.0=V1, 3.26.0=V2) on php:8.2-cli; guard = a real Twig Environment + SandboxExtension + SecurityPolicy allow-list. Sink = SecurityPolicy allow-list enforcement on a sandbox-included template already cached (loaded once outside the sandbox). Canary = benign SSTI: a non-allow-listed Twig function pcb_flag() that echoes ${PCB_FLAG} from the HOST process env; reaching it proves the allow-list was skipped. Seed (CVE-2024-45411) = sandboxed include() FUNCTION of a cached name; residual (CVE-2026-46638) = {% sandbox %}{% include %} TAG on the same cached template. Variant A gate (validate_case) + V2 negative control both pass. Mechanism derived from the advisory + the real twig source diffs (patch.diff); no public offensive PoC used. RELATIONSHIP VERDICT: genuine incomplete fix (advisory title explicitly 'incomplete fix for CVE-2024-45411'). SSTI/template-sandbox-escape class -- previously absent from the benchmark. Composer 2 advisory-block policy is disabled in the Dockerfile because the pinned twig versions are intentionally vulnerable.
